Sara (CS): Kicking off SmoothShore dedicated pool bring-up. Need to lock quota, autoscale policy, and final load test windows. T-minus ~72h to handoff. tagging @Alex (Solutions) and @Tom (Ops) for capacity playbook :rocket:
Tom (Ops): Thanks — can we confirm committed quota (GPUs / vCPU) + a warmup tolerance? SmoothShore committed 8 GPUs but asked for burst to 12 for first 48h.
Alex (Solutions): Confirmed 8 reserved gpus, burst policy needs autoscale config. Proposed policy: min_instances=2 max_instances=6 burst_quota=4. Will that map to their 8->12 ask?
Julia (SRE): We map GPUs->instances differently. For this fleet, 1 instance = 2 GPUs. So min=2 -> 4 GPUs, max=6 -> 12 GPUs. That matches requested 8->12 if we prime to 4 instances during ramp.
Sara (CS): OK good. Next: load test timeline. SmoothShore prefers CET evening window. Can we run smoke + soak tomorrow 18:00 CET?
Tom (Ops): I can run smoke + soak at that time. Need the load profile and k6 script. Also flag to ops: KV cache priming must run before soak.
Alex (Solutions): Sharing traffic profile (small):
```
- 10m smoke: ramp 0->200 rps
- 60m soak: steady 800 rps (95th p99 target < 250ms)
- prefix cache priming: replay 5k unique warmup requests
```
Sara (CS): Adding notes: run prefix priming 30m before soak, then start soak. We'll capture output for quality checks.
Julia (SRE): Ops checklist for test run:
  • Ensure pool ss-2026 has quota pinned
  • Set autoscale policy: target_qps=800 target_latency_ms=200 scale_cooldown=120s
  • Enable fallback route to hosted-tier for error budget > 5%
Tom (Ops): I'll push the autoscale policy to staging now. Command: `rictl apply --pool ss-2026 --policy autoscale-smoothshore-v1`
deploy-bot: env-provision: pool ss-2026 created (region: eu-central-1) — resources: 6 instances (12 GPUs) staged for tests
Sara (CS): Nice. One more ask from SmoothShore: data routing must be private for the soak run (no logs leave project). Alex, can you confirm KMS/HSM key used?
Alex (Solutions): Confirmed KMS key ss-shore-kms in their VPC; logs will be retained per their policy.
Julia (SRE): Also recommend running a canary ramp: 10% traffic (80 rps) -> 50% (400 rps) -> 100% (800 rps) over 15m increments to verify cache behavior.
Tom (Ops): Will do. I'll also capture token-level cost delta and latency buckets. Can someone attach the monitoring dashboard link here?
Sara (CS): Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/ss-2026/smoothshore-load (use case tag: smoothshore-bringup)
Alex (Solutions): I'll own customer enablement: provide runbook to SmoothShore post-test + guide for rollback.
Sara (CS): Post-test checklist: capture error traces, compare regression prompts, and surface any alignment issues to PMs. If p99 > 400ms, we hold on go-live.
Julia (SRE): Noted. If error rate spikes > 3% for longer than 5m, autoscale will try to add instances; if capacity exhausted, routing fallback will shift 20% to hosted-api.
Tom (Ops): All set from infra side. I'll start priming at 17:20 CET, smoke at 18:00 CET, soak 18:15 CET. Will paste test logs here.
Sara (CS): Perfect. SmoothShore requested a short dry-run with them at 16:00 CET earlier today — Alex and I did that and only minor latency jitter. Good to proceed. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: loadtest-run: ID lt-ss-4387 queued by Tom (Ops) — results will post to thread on completion
Tom (Ops): Kicking off priming now.
Sara (CS): Thanks team — ping me if anything blocks. I'll update the customer scoreboard after soak.
Tom (Ops): 18:28 CET update: soak stable at 800 rps, p95 180ms, p99 260ms, error rate 0.6%. Uploading artifacts...
Sara (CS): Copy. I'll schedule a short sync with SmoothShore at 09:00 CET tomorrow to review the results and next steps.
